_comment: Repo-tracked CURATED catalog for Higgs Audio v3 narration voices — the Higgs counterpart of orpheus-models.json, and deliberately NOT the same shape where the two engines differ. Orpheus's catalog OVERLAYS a per-machine runtime install manifest because Orpheus voices are folder-discovered. Higgs has no folder discovery: a Higgs voice is a row in THIS FILE, so there is no runtime manifest and no reconcile fallback — a voice that is not listed here does not exist, and higgs-models.ts refuses it BY NAME rather than falling through to the served model's own speaker (which measures at 12% of the narrator's ECAPA ceiling: a DIFFERENT person, not a weak clone). Every number in a backends block is MEASURED — provenance in E:\training\_campaigns\2026-09-01-cod-full-rebuild\higgs\HIGGS_V3_LEVERS.md — or is an explicitly-marked placeholder that the loader REFUSES to render with. AND THERE IS ONE BLOCK PER BACKEND, not one per voice: `served` is vllm-omni behind WSL, `mlx` is the in-process mlx-audio sampler on the Mac, and the loader picks by ARM (wsl -> served, darwin -> mlx). They do not share numbers, because a cap is produced by RENDERING and the two arms sample through different implementations of top-k/top-p over different runtimes -- the same three sampling values make the configuration identical, not the draws (PORT_NOTES 13.11). So copying a merged directory to the other machine copies the WEIGHTS and not the CERTIFICATE; see _checkpointShapeComment and the deathstalker entry, whose mlx cap is null while its served cap is being measured.
_wireFormatComment: THIS FILE IS NOT THE WIRE FORMAT. narrator reads a VOICE DOCUMENT whose path arrives in NARRATOR_HIGGS_VOICES (see python/narrator/engine/higgs/config.py load_voices): `{ "<voiceId>": { "clips": [{path, transcript, seconds}], "scene"?, "adapterDir"?, "allowedControls"?, "maxReferenceSeconds"? } }`. In THAT format a Higgs voice is ALWAYS clips, and a fine-tune is an `checkpointDir` riding on the same object — there is no separate checkpoint kind. This catalog keeps an explicit `kind` anyway, because `kind` is what selects BOOKFORGE'S OWN RULES (above all: maxChars is REQUIRED and measured for an adapter, and may be the engine placeholder for a zero-shot voice) and because a picker has to tell a person which of the two they are choosing. `higgsVoicesDocument()` in higgs-models.ts translates one into the other; it is the only place the two shapes meet.
_licenseComment: Higgs Audio v3 (bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b) ships under the Boson Higgs TTS 3 RESEARCH AND NON-COMMERCIAL license, and a fine-tune of those weights INHERITS it. That is why every entry carries an explicit `license` and `commercialUse: false`: this engine is enabled for Owen's personal evaluation and cannot ship in a commercial BookForge build without a separate licence from Boson AI. Higgs Audio v2 is the trainable-and-shippable family (Community licence: attribution plus 'Higgs Audio 2' in any fine-tune's name) and is NOT in this catalog — Owen dropped v2 on 2026-09-04 ('basically just Orpheus and we know Orpheus better').
_checkpointFilesComment: THE REQUIRED FILES OF A kind:checkpoint VOICE LIVE IN ITS checkpointDir, not in this catalog, and one of them is easy to lose: generation_config.json. vllm-omni serve resolves sampling FROM THE MODEL DIRECTORY (--generation-config defaults to auto), so that file IS the temperature/top_p/top_k every request is answered at; a merged dir without it falls through to the bare SamplingParams() in vllm_omni entrypoints/openai/stage_params.py — top_p 1.0, top_k DISABLED — which samples the untruncated 1026-way codebook tail and derails prompts over ~600 chars into babble (measured 2026-09-05). OpenAICreateSpeechRequest carries no sampling fields, so nothing per-request can correct it. PROVENANCE: bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b ships NO generation_config.json (verified across the whole WSL HF cache and the Mac base snapshot) — the MERGE writes one into every merged dir from a recorded runs/<run>/generation_config.override.json whose values are vllm-omni own deploy/higgs_multimodal_qwen3.yaml stage-0 default_sampling_params ({temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 50, repetition_penalty 1.0}), recording the source in merge_manifest.json beside the weights. So a checkpointDir must carry: the weights, config.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja AND generation_config.json. BookForge does NOT check this — the directory is inside WSL (or on the Mac) and this process cannot see it; narrator refuses BY NAME at load (v3_served.require_generation_config, reached through checkpoint_serve_target) on absence, unparseable JSON, or a file carrying none of temperature/top_p/top_k. On the Mac that file is narrator OWN sampling too: mlx-audio 0.4.8 does not read it and its Model.generate defaults top_p/top_k to None. See docs/HIGGS_ENGINE.md and python/narrator/engine/PORT_NOTES.md 12.8d + 13.11.
_referenceComment: EXACTLY ONE REFERENCE CLIP PER VOICE, 30 s of audio at the very most. vllm-omni refuses multi-shot cloning, so 'two clips' means ONE pre-joined wav (clips joined by 0.35 s of silence) whose transcript is the transcripts joined in the same order — the joining happens when the voice is STAGED, never at render time, and this catalog stores the joined result. Every clip must declare its `seconds`: narrator's v3_served.reference_seconds refuses a clip without one rather than probing the file, so a missing duration is a render that dies after the server has already spent five minutes coming up. Measured: no reference 0.093 speaker cosine, one clip 0.680, two joined 0.692, against a 0.766 narrator self-ceiling — and same-book-vs-cross-book is worth +0.076 where the second clip is worth only +0.012, so a reference set must come from ONE book.

serving._comment: The shared v3 serving stack, selected by a model's engineVersion. A model entry may declare its own `serving` block, used INSTEAD of this one (never field-merged) so a voice has exactly one serving answer. narrator INVOKES the operator's launch script rather than writing its own — the CUDA_HOME/FlashInfer workarounds live there and a second copy would drift — so `launchScript` is what NARRATOR_HIGGS3_SERVE_SCRIPT points at.
serving._deployConfigNote: A vllm-omni deploy profile, reaching the launcher as HIGGS_DEPLOY_CONFIG. It is a FILE NAME or a full path, NEVER a bare profile name: measured 2026-09-05, vllm-omni 0.28.0 resolves `--deploy-config <bare name>` to "Deploy config not found" (config_factory._load_user_deploy_config joins a bare name to the deploy dir without appending .yaml), and both the launcher and higgsSpawnEnv refuse a bare name before the launch rather than paying a 297 s cold start to read the crash. IT IS NO LONGER null. THE VALUE HERE IS A BARE FILE NAME AND BookForge RESOLVES IT: higgsSpawnEnv emits HIGGS_DEPLOY_CONFIG=<wsl conda base>/envs/<higgs env>/bin/higgs_default_frames7500.yaml — the SAME derivation that produces NARRATOR_HIGGS3_SERVE_SCRIPT, so the profile that runs is the installer's copy sitting beside the launcher and not whatever a relative name would resolve against in vllm-omni's own deploy directory. A value written here WITH a path separator is passed through verbatim instead. WHY A PROFILE IS SET AT ALL: see _frameCeilingNote — the auto-discovered profile caps every render at 2048 frames (81.92 s) and no request parameter can raise it. This is NOT the CUDA-graph question: higgs_multimodal_qwen3_low_latency.yaml (enforce_eager false, cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY) is a separate profile and still uncertified.
serving._frameCeilingNote: THE SERVED SPEECH ENDPOINT IGNORES A PER-REQUEST max_tokens, so stage 0's `default_sampling_params.max_tokens` in the deploy profile is a HARD CEILING on the audio length of EVERY render. MEASURED 2026-09-05 (owens-pc, RTX 3090 Ti, vllm-omni 0.28.0): vllm-omni's auto-discovered higgs_multimodal_qwen3.yaml sets it to 2048 frames = 81.92 s, and a chunk needing more audio than that is CUT MID-SENTENCE — silently, with the request reporting success. Raising it per request does nothing; the profile is the only lever. electron/scripts/higgs/higgs_default_frames7500.yaml is byte-identical to that auto profile EXCEPT max_tokens 7500 (300 s), which is what this block's deployConfig names. THE FILE'S BYTES ARE THE BINDING: the training side's certificates were measured against sha256 24d288f193eaa8c5…, so that file is edited by re-certifying and never in place — the installer copies it into <env>/bin/ on every run and the doctor's `profile-sha` row compares the deployed copy against the shipped one. It is a FILE rather than a write into site-packages because a pip upgrade in the env reverts site-packages (that is what reverts the two patches above) and cannot revert a profile passed on the command line.
serving._servingNote: EVERY FIELD IN THIS BLOCK NOW REACHES THE LAUNCH SCRIPT, and until 2026-09-05 none of them did. electron/higgs-models.ts:higgsSpawnEnv emitted only the NARRATOR_* set, so electron/scripts/higgs/serve_higgs_v3.sh ran on its own built-in defaults and this block was a description of a configuration nothing applied — editing maxNumSeqs here changed nothing at all, which is worse than having no field, because it is a lever that reports success. The route is now: higgsServingFor(model) -> higgsSpawnEnv -> HIGGS_* environment -> buildNarratorSpawn's `export K=V` prefix into the guest -> the worker's env -> serve_higgs_v3.sh. The mapping, one per line: host -> HIGGS_HOST, port -> HIGGS_PORT, gpuMemoryUtilization -> HIGGS_GPU_MEM_UTIL, codecGpuMemoryUtilization -> HIGGS_CODEC_GPU_MEM_UTIL, maxModelLen -> HIGGS_MAX_MODEL_LEN, maxNumSeqs -> HIGGS_MAX_NUM_SEQS, deployConfig -> HIGGS_DEPLOY_CONFIG (emitted only when it is not null, and RESOLVED TO AN ABSOLUTE GUEST PATH when it is a bare file name — see _deployConfigNote), plus HIGGS_ENV, which is the conda prefix the spawn derives and the script builds CUDA_HOME/PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH from. TWO OF THEM ARE NOT ONLY THE SCRIPT'S: narrator re-exports HIGGS_HOST/HIGGS_PORT/HIGGS_MAX_NUM_SEQS into the wrapper it launches (v3_served.py _launch_exports), so the pair that binds and the pair narrator polls cannot drift, and serve_concurrency() sizes narrator's own batch from HIGGS_MAX_NUM_SEQS and REFUSES BY NAME when it is unset — which is why BookForge sets that one on every arm and every phase, not just where a server is started. HIGGS_MODEL_DIR is the exception in the other direction: narrator exports it per voice from the voice document's checkpointDir, so BookForge must never set it. A missing or out-of-range number here is REFUSED by name in higgsSpawnEnv rather than defaulted — these land on a vllm-omni command line five minutes before anything can be heard.
serving._maxNumSeqsNote: 16 is vllm-omni's OWN profile value for stage 0 (higgs_multimodal_qwen3.yaml), and it replaced a 2 that was never anything but a placeholder — it reached nothing until 2026-09-05, so no measurement was ever taken against it. IT IS NOW ALSO A MEASURED CEILING AT THE SHIPPED MEMORY FRACTIONS: on owens-pc (RTX 3090 Ti, 2026-09-05) 16 concurrent at 0.35 + 0.10 ran 11,387-11,584 chars/min over three runs while 32 concurrent filled the card and stalled. THE CERTIFYING SERVER FOR deathstalker RAN AT 64 (see that voice's served _maxCharsNote) — at the OLD fractions and before that stall was measured — so 16 is not the width its cap was certified at. Nothing measured says whether batch width moves the safe chunk length; if it does, the deathstalker certificate is bound to 64 and this is the field that would have to change. It is also the width of narrator's own batch (serve_concurrency), so raising it raises concurrent POSTs and VRAM pressure together.
serving._coldStartNote: 297 s from launch to /health answering, MEASURED on narrator's own GPU smoke (2026-09-04) — not the ~55 s the first audition reported, which was a warm cache. narrator's READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 300, i.e. the measurement sits three seconds under the limit. Anything in BookForge that decides a Higgs job is dead must therefore allow AT LEAST five minutes before the first audio. Checked against the two that could: WORKER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS is 10 minutes and WORKER_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS is 12 (parallel-tts-bridge.ts), so both already clear it — but they clear it by minutes, not by an order of magnitude, and anyone tightening them must re-read this line. THE SERVER PREALLOCATES AND THEN OWNS THE CARD, in TWO STAGES, each fraction passed PER STAGE through --stage-overrides (vllm-omni applies a GLOBAL --gpu-memory-utilization to EVERY stage — omni_config.py _stage_cli_overrides — so the campaign's single `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.60` reserved 0.60 TWICE, measured holding 24.2 GB of a 24.5 GB card; the same flag was also clamping the codec stage's context length to maxModelLen 8192 against its profile's 65536). AND THE TALKER'S FRACTION IS ITS KV CACHE BUDGET ON TOP OF THE WEIGHTS, NOT A CAP ON THE STAGE — the server's own log at 0.35 (owens-pc, 2026-09-05): "Desired GPU memory utilization is (0.35, 8.4 GiB). Actual usage is 7.72 GiB", "Available KV cache memory: 8.4 GiB", "GPU KV cache size: 61,120 tokens". Reading it as a ceiling is what overcommitted the card. MEASURED, same box, same night: 0.60 + 0.25 held 24,274 MiB with the WDDM driver paging into shared system RAM and the render falling from ~8 to ~2 chunks/min; 0.55 + 0.15 held 24.0 GB and still paged; 0.35 + 0.10 holds 18.7-19.2 GB with IDENTICAL THROUGHPUT at 16 concurrent — 11,387-11,584 chars/min across three runs — which is why those are the shipped values. 32 concurrent at 0.35 + 0.10 filled the card and stalled.
serving._flashInferNote: FlashInfer is unavailable on sm_86 with torch 2.13+cu130 — it JIT-builds its attention kernels with nvcc and its bundled CCCL headers reject the CUDA 13 nvcc from the pip wheel — so the launch pins VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0, VLLM_DISABLE_FLASHINFER_PREFILL=1 and --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN. Speed only; the flashinfer-jit-cache cu130/sm_86 wheel from https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130/torch2.13/ is the route if v3 speed ever matters.

patches.why: vLLM 0.28's blanket negative-token-id rejection fires on vllm-omni's AUDIO_PLACEHOLDER_ID (-100), which the clone path deliberately emits for the talker to substitute reference embeddings at prefill. Without the patch EVERY clone request is HTTP 400 'Token id -100 is out of vocabulary' — which is what made cloning look broken in the first audition.

Upstream substitutes every out-of-range code with 0 and then trims exactly ONE frame. Both halves are wrong: 0 is a VALID codec code, so the substitution CONVERTS the ramp-down BOC/EOC sentinels into real sound rather than neutralising them; and the sentinels smear across the last Q-1 = 7 frames (codebook c is delayed by c positions), so one frame leaves ~240 ms of audible garbage at the end of every chunk — Owen heard it as 'a stray syllable or sound after each sentence'. The patch decides by TOKEN IDENTITY instead: a frame is kept iff all 8 codebooks are in [0, 1023], nothing out of range ever reaches the codec, and there is no substitution and no positional trim left. The sync path gets the full filter; the streaming path gets the trailing run only, because Stage 1 trims left_context/right_holdback BY FRAME COUNT and dropping a leading or interior frame there would desync those trims and cut real speech. IT IS SERVER-SIDE: a patched server returns an already-clean tail and THE CLIENT MUST NOT TRIM AGAIN — what is left is a hard sample boundary, which is the assembler's 10/25 ms fade job. SUPERSEDES patch_tail_trim.py (retired 2026-09-05), which walked backwards from the end while frames were bad — positional reasoning that kept the 0-substitution for every sentinel outside the trailing run.
patches._markerNote: The marker is `_filter_sentinel_frames` and NOT `_trim_trailing_sentinel_frames`: this patch writes BOTH helpers (the trailing-run one is what the streaming path calls), and the retired patch_tail_trim.py wrote the trailing-run one too — so grepping for that would certify a band-aided file as patched. `absentMarker` is the other half of the proof and is asserted to be ABSENT: `[:, :-1]` is upstream's one-frame trim, which occurs twice in the pristine file and zero times after this patch (measured on the certifying box, vllm-omni 0.28.0, 2026-09-05). Present marker + absent trim is exactly 'the token-identity filter is in and no trim code remains', which is the half of the patch's proof that can be checked statically.
patches._certifiedShaNote: The stage processor this patch produces, on vllm-omni 0.28.0, is sha256 0b36f6507dd11653253bbebb278c3657e5d17a2a52f78018cd0bddd45a7ac210 (pristine: 376ca5647773cb191634b266b03bfefe490c080ef9f75aed045f1f31c9a19fb4), and the repo's electron/scripts/higgs/patch_sentinel_filter.py reproduces it byte for byte from the pristine file — verified 2026-09-05. THAT SHA IS PART OF A CERTIFICATE: a certificate binds (checkpoint dir, stage-processor sha, max_chars) together, so a change to this patch is a new server build that re-certifies rather than inheriting a published cap. See docs/HIGGS_ENGINE.md.

serving._voiceSwitchNote: A VOICE SWITCH IS A SERVER RESTART, and that is not a tuning choice — it is the only thing vllm-omni supports. It cannot load a LoRA at runtime: there are no adapter flags on `vllm-omni serve`, and the higgs_audio_v3 talker class does not implement SupportsLoRA. So every Higgs voice ships as a MERGED CHECKPOINT DIRECTORY (~8.5 GB) and the server is started ON that directory. Switching voice costs a restart: ~55 s warm (page cache hot) to ~300 s cold, against the 300 s readyTimeoutSeconds. A book renders in ONE voice, so this is paid once per job and never per chunk — but anything that imagined mixing voices within a render, or a cheap per-request voice cast, cannot be built on this stack.

models.label: Higgs v3 built-in voice (no reference)

served._maxCharsNote: 600 is the ZERO-SHOT figure and it is measured, not guessed: coverage by faster-whisper/difflib alignment is 1.000 at 213/440/504 chars and holds through 600, while 898 chars fails REPRODUCIBLY (coverage 0.86 and 0.78 on two seeds; tail coverage 0.314 and 0.000 — it drops the end of the paragraph). A reference clip does NOT fix it; it is a v3 model property that v2 does not have. DURATION RATIO IS NOT A COVERAGE PROXY: at temperature 0.7 the 898-char chunk produced ratio 0.99 while actually delivering coverage 0.778 with a 26% insert rate — it dropped text and padded the duration with hallucinated words, and any cap built on duration alone would have passed it. THIS NUMBER IS VALID ONLY FOR ZERO-SHOT and must never be copied onto an adapter voice; see the deathstalker entry.
served._edgeFadeNote: WHO APPLIES THIS: narrator's assembler, and as of narrator 4854aae4 it DOES — assemble/engine_profiles.py declares higgs-v3 as pads=false with 10/25 ms fades, assemble/edges.py applies them as RAISED-COSINE windows (zero slope at both ends, so the join has no discontinuity in the first derivative either), and _plan_unpadded realizes the manifest gapBefore/gapAfter as generated silence through one FLAC writer so the concat stays homogeneous. Prep writes the gaps.json sidecar these read, and session_v1 REFUSES a pads=false session without it. An earlier draft of parallel-tts-bridge.ts justified routing Higgs assembly to narrator by claiming narrator already read this field when neither side did; it does now, and the number is here because the catalog is where per-voice tuning lives. WHY THE FADE IS NEEDED AT ALL: Higgs emits NO lead/trail silence of its own — unlike Orpheus, which bakes pads into each chunk FLAC — and the patched server already trims its own sentinel tail, so what reaches the assembler ends at a hard sample boundary: a step discontinuity, i.e. a click. 25 ms out / 10 ms in removes it, taking a chunk edge from about -30 dB to -45..-48 dB. Applied at ASSEMBLY and never baked into the per-chunk wav, so the raw model output stays inspectable. This is also why the manifest gapBefore/gapAfter are LIVE for Higgs where they are inert for Orpheus.
served._samplingNote: The server's OWN shipped defaults (vllm_omni/deploy/higgs_multimodal_qwen3.yaml, stage 0 default_sampling_params), and the delivered render sends NO extra_params at all so they apply verbatim. Written down here anyway so the value that renders is stated rather than inherited invisibly from a yaml inside site-packages. TWO TRAPS: (1) temperature/top_p/top_k are NOT fields of OpenAICreateSpeechRequest — sent at the request top level pydantic DROPS them silently and the render runs at 1.0/0.95/50 regardless, which is exactly how the first audition reported 0.3 while running at 1.0; they must ride inside `extra_params`. (2) Deviations were measured (temp 0.3/0.7/1.0 at top_p 0.95 gave cosine 0.653/0.675/0.642 at 368 chars) and the spread is INSIDE single-seed noise — two seeds of the same setting differ by 0.04 — so one seed per cell cannot rank them and none beat the default enough to leave it.
served._allowedControlsNote: EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and it is a safety rule rather than a preference. An inline control token that is NOT in get_added_vocab() is split into 7-10 ordinary text pieces and READ ALOUD, which derails generation into a degenerate loop: ASR coverage 0.000, pitch std collapsing to 0.28 st, speaker cosine 0.05. A typo is not ignored — it destroys the render. v3 also has NO scene-description mechanism (<|scene_desc_start|> is a v2 chat role, absent from v3's vocabulary) and no `neutral`/`calm` emotion. At default sampling no control token beat plain text on speaker cosine, and the one candidate (<|prosody:long_pause|>) did not change measured pause density. The delivered render uses none. An empty allowlist means no engine ever has to get the validation right.

mlx._comment: THE MAC'S OWN BLOCK. A CERTIFICATE IS PER (DIRECTORY, BACKEND), so this is not `served` copied across — every field here is stated for the mlx-audio sampler, which is a different implementation of top-k/top-p over a different runtime from vllm-omni's (PORT_NOTES 13.11). The loader picks the block by ARM (wsl -> served, darwin -> mlx) and refuses a fine-tune whose block carries a null cap.
mlx._maxCharsNote: THE SAME PLACEHOLDER ON BOTH ARMS, AND THAT IS NOT AN INHERITANCE. A placeholder makes no claim about a backend — it is the zero-shot figure the v3 family was measured at on the served path, and it is labelled `placeholder` precisely so nobody reads it as a certificate. It may therefore be stated twice where a MEASURED number may not: narrator's own HiggsV3Defaults.MAX_CHARS is 600 on both arms too, so all three agree by construction rather than by copying. What must NEVER be stated twice is a length-sweep number, which is why deathstalker's mlx cap is null.
mlx._edgeFadeNote: SAME CODEC, SAME NUMBERS, and applied by the same code: narrator's assembler (assemble/engine_profiles.py declares higgs-v3 as pads=false with 10/25 ms raised-cosine fades) runs on whichever arm rendered. The fade is a property of the DECODED WAVEFORM's hard sample boundary, not of the sampler that produced the tokens, so unlike maxChars it genuinely does not vary by backend.
mlx._samplingNote: STATED, NOT MIRRORED — because there is no file to mirror. The bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b snapshot ships NO generation_config.json (verified on the WSL HF cache and on the Mac's runtime/higgs-models/base, 2026-09-05), which is the whole reason a MERGED directory has to carry one. So for BASE weights the authority is v3's documented deploy default, v3_served.SERVER_DEFAULT_SAMPLING, which is what narrator's HiggsV3MlxConfig.mlx_sampling() applies here and what the served arm sends in extra_params for the same weights. mlx-audio itself reads no such file and its Model.generate defaults top_p/top_k to None -- i.e. the untruncated codebook tail -- so narrator passing these three is the only thing that makes the two arms render the base model alike.
mlx._referenceSecondsCapNote: The vllm-omni server's 30 s HTTP limit is enforced on THIS arm too, by narrator: HiggsV3MlxConfig calls v3_served.check_reference_budget, and HiggsV3Defaults.MAX_REFERENCE_SECONDS is 30.0 for both. Stated rather than omitted so a clips voice auditioned on the Mac is refused at the same length the server would refuse it at.

models.note: The model's own voice with no reference audio at all. MEASURED at ECAPA speaker cosine 0.0929 against the deathstalker narrator — 12% of that narrator's own 0.7656 self-consistency ceiling — i.e. it is a DIFFERENT SPEAKER, not a weak clone. It is listed because it is the one Higgs voice that needs nothing staged on disk, so it is what a machine can audition the serving stack with before any clone or fine-tune exists. Do not narrate a book in it expecting a particular narrator.
models._kindNote: kind default — THE SERVED MODEL'S OWN VOICE, and a distinct shape rather than an empty clips list. narrator refuses a ClipsVoice with zero clips, and it is right to: a zero-shot clone with NO reference is not a degenerate clone, it is a different thing entirely — the model's built-in speaker, which measures at 12% of the deathstalker narrator's ECAPA ceiling. An earlier draft of this catalog wrote `clips: []` for it and called that 'the served default voice', which made the two indistinguishable in the wire format and would have been refused by name.

models.label: Deathstalker (Higgs v3 fine-tune)
models._targetCharsNote: THE CHUNK SIZE THE CODE PACKS TO, PER ARM (backends.served.targetChars / backends.mlx.targetChars), set by the trainer after training from the training clips' text lengths. Owen, 2026-09-05: 'maxChars is what the model was trained to do, and targetChars can be what the system actually uses. maxChars is informative, targetChars is used by the code directly.' The prep's cap AND merge floor: consecutive short paragraphs travel together until the next would overflow it, a paragraph already at it stands alone, walls stay walls. Never above the arm's maxChars - both sides refuse that by name. A fine-tune with no targetChars cannot be prepped. INTERIM VALUES (Owen, 2026-09-05 evening: 'set it to deathstalker's theoretical maximum of about 80 seconds'): each arm's certified maximum - served 1200 (~71 s at the measured 5.9 audio-s per 100 chars; the served sweep dropped text at 1500), MLX 900 (its sweep dropped text at 1200). MEASURED the same evening on both arms: this checkpoint ENDS ITSELF at ~1,980 frames (~79-82 s) whatever the server ceiling - a 2,173-char render on the Mac gave 79 s with the middle skipped (coverage 0.306) - so no target above ~1,350 chars can work on this checkpoint; the retrain that favours longer clips states its own numbers here, with the method in targetCharsSource.
models._checkpointArmNote: TWO ARMS, TWO COPIES, TWO CERTIFICATES — and this entry names both because a checkpoint voice is ~8.5 GB on disk and the arms cannot see each other's disks. `wsl` is the merged directory inside the WSL guest, which is what serve_higgs_v3.sh is started on; `darwin` is the SAME merged directory copied onto the Mac, written RELATIVE to the app's userData (it resolves to /Users/<account>/Library/Application Support/BookForge/runtime/higgs-models/ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080, beside the `base` weights the MLX backend already loads from). The Mac copy was staged 2026-09-05 and carries the same file set (model.safetensors, config.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja, generation_config.json, merge_manifest.json). WHY THE darwin ENTRY IS RELATIVE AND THE wsl ONE IS NOT: the guest has a fixed home and hands its path straight to a launch script, while a Mac's Application Support path carries the ACCOUNT NAME — an absolute /Users/telltale/... in a repo-tracked catalog is a directory that exists on exactly one machine, which is the failure this catalog exists to prevent (see _cloneFallbackNote for the same rule applied to reference clips). The app knows its own userData; the catalog does not, so higgsVoicesDocument() joins them at document-write time and the wire format still carries ONE absolute `checkpointDir`. AN ARM WITH NO ENTRY IS NOT A GAP TO FILL FROM THE OTHER ONE: the voice is simply not loadable there, refused by name ('is not staged for the Mac: no darwin checkpoint in the catalog'), and the narration dropdown greys it out on that machine. AND A COPY IS A NEW CERTIFICATE, NOT AN INHERITED ONE — see backends: the cap is per (directory, BACKEND), and the MLX sampler is a different implementation of top-k/top-p over a different runtime from vllm-omni's, so the same three numbers make the configuration identical and not the draws (PORT_NOTES 13.11).
models._checkpointDirNote: NOT the /home/<user>/higgs-models/<voice>/ convention the installer creates, and NOT interchangeable with the sibling directory beside it. A CERTIFICATE BINDS (checkpoint dir, stage-processor patch sha, max_chars) TOGETHER: a cap is measured by rendering against ONE directory on ONE patched server, so it is that triple that is certified and never the number alone. Two merges of the same run are two directories and two certificates. WHAT IS ON DISK (2026-09-05): /home/telltale/higgs_v3_merged/ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080 — ckpt-1080, the LOWEST-LOSS checkpoint, chosen by Owen after an ear test, and what this entry names; CERTIFIED 2026-09-05T12:52:57 at max_chars 1200 against this directory, its generation_config.json and the patched stage processor 0b36f650 — certificate at E:\training\_campaigns\2026-09-01-cod-full-rebuild\higgs\v3_ft\logs\max_chars_certificate_ckpt1080.json. And /home/telltale/higgs_v3_merged/ds_ad4lm_prod — ckpt-480, the rule-picked one, kept as the ALTERNATE and carrying its own certificate (max_chars 1200, certified 2026-09-05 against that directory and the patched stage processor 0b36f650…). THAT CERTIFICATE IS NOT THIS DIRECTORY'S: nothing here, in narrator or in vllm-omni compares two directories' weights or generation_config.json byte for byte, so a number carried across would be inherited without its measurement. BOTH ARE FROZEN: a re-merge or a recipe change writes a NEW directory name and re-certifies; since 2026-09-05 a merged directory may not be RENAMED either, and certification asserts that a directory's merge_manifest.out names ITSELF. HIGGS_MODELS_DIR in install_higgs_env.sh still describes where a voice MAY be staged; it is not where this one is, and moving it would mean running the sweep again. PROVENANCE CORRECTION, kept as history because a stale path string is exactly how two merged directories stop being distinguishable. FOUND 2026-09-05: this directory's merge_manifest.json recorded "out": "/home/telltale/higgs_v3_merged/ds_ad4lm_prod" — its SIBLING's path — and its generation_config.json said "_written_by": "backfilled 2026-09-05 for ds_ad4lm_prod". CAUSE: it was merged TO the path ds_ad4lm_prod and RENAMED to ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080 when ckpt-480 took the ds_ad4lm_prod name — so the path strings were stale, and only the path strings. CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-09-05T10:35:56 by the training side: both files now name THIS directory, each carries a timestamped `provenance_correction` recording the rename, and the original value is KEPT rather than overwritten (merge_manifest `out_original_at_merge_time`). CONFIRMED by re-reading both files read-only, 2026-09-05: `out` and `_written_by` name ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080, `lora` is still runs/ds_ad4lm_prod/ckpt-1080 on snapshot 239f63fb…, sampling is still 1.0 / 0.95 / 50 / 1.0, and model.safetensors' mtime is unchanged (08:08) against the two JSONs' 10:35 — the weights were not touched. The two guards above are what came out of it; the catalog path is still what says which weights render, but it is no longer the ONLY thing, because the directory now names itself.

served._maxCharsNote: 1200, CERTIFIED for THIS directory — /home/telltale/higgs_v3_merged/ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080 — on 2026-09-05T12:52:57 by the Higgs fine-tuning session. Certificate: E:\training\_campaigns\2026-09-01-cod-full-rebuild\higgs\v3_ft\logs\max_chars_certificate_ckpt1080.json (read read-only when this was written). THE RULE, quoted from the file: "babble==0 across all seeds AND min per-seed coverage>=0.90, contiguous from the shortest tested length". Scored by ASR alignment and never by duration ratio — a v3 render measured ratio 0.99 while dropping 22 % of its text. THE LADDER, from the certificate's contiguous_pass: 150, 300, 600, 900, 1200 — five lengths passing without a gap, and 1200 is the last of them. PER-LENGTH FIGURES reported by the session with the number: babble 0/4 seeds at 600 / 900 / 1200, minimum per-seed coverage 99.2 % / 97.1 % / 97.3 %; 1500 FAILS at 86.1 % — on COVERAGE, not on babble, which is the same shape the ckpt-480 sweep found. WHAT THE NUMBER IS BOUND TO, all of it recorded in the certificate's bound_to: the checkpoint dir above (whose merge_manifest.out names ITSELF — asserted at certify time), lora runs/ds_ad4lm_prod/ckpt-1080 on base snapshot 239f63fb…, the directory's generation_config.json {temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 50, repetition_penalty 1.0}, and THE SERVER BUILD: stage-input-processor sha256 0b36f6507dd11653, the token-identity sentinel filter (patch_sentinel_filter.py), vllm/vllm-omni 0.28.0. Change any of those and this number is not certified for what is running — see _checkpointDirNote. OBSERVED, and recorded rather than smoothed over: the certifying server ran with --max-num-seqs 64 while this catalog's shared serving block declares maxNumSeqs 2. Nothing measured says whether batch width moves the safe chunk length; it is stated so that a reader comparing the two does not assume they were the same server. WHY THIS FIELD MAY NEVER BE INHERITED: a fine-tuned Higgs checkpoint's stop length tracks its TRAINING CLIP LENGTH rather than the text it is given — a 30-minute adapter trained on 8-22 s clips stopped after ~6-10 s of audio on any prompt over ~150 characters — so the zero-shot 600 is wrong for a fine-tune in the direction that LOSES TEXT while every duration check still looks plausible. The sibling directory ds_ad4lm_prod (ckpt-480) is certified at 1200 too; that the two agree is a RESULT, not a reason — each was measured against its own weights.
served._samplingNote: A MIRROR, AND THE DIRECTORY IS THE AUTHORITY. What answers every request is /home/telltale/higgs_v3_merged/ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080/generation_config.json — vllm-omni resolves sampling from the MODEL DIRECTORY (--generation-config defaults to auto) and OpenAICreateSpeechRequest carries no sampling fields, so nothing per-request can correct it; narrator PROVES that file is there (v3_served.require_generation_config) and never writes one. Read on 2026-09-05 it holds {"temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 50, "repetition_penalty": 1.0, "_source": "stage-0 default_sampling_params from higgs_multimodal_qwen3.yaml"} — the same four numbers as the ckpt-480 directory, which is expected: both were written from the same recorded per-run override. The three are mirrored here so a reader can see what this voice samples at without opening a directory inside WSL, and tools/test-higgs-engine.js asserts the mirror still matches — a mirror nobody checks is how two copies of a number diverge. If they ever disagree, the DIRECTORY wins and this block is what is wrong.
served._maxCharsSourceNote: `length-sweep` is a TOKEN, not the provenance. maxCharsSource TRAVELS into narrator's voice document, where `protocol.MAX_CHARS_SOURCES` is a CLOSED vocabulary — catalog | placeholder | length-sweep — and anything else is refused by name at load_voices. So the method's NAME rides the wire and the measurement itself stays here, in _maxCharsNote, which narrator never sees.

mlx._comment: THE MAC'S OWN BLOCK FOR THIS FINE-TUNE, and it is UNCERTIFIED. The merged directory was copied to the Mac on 2026-09-05 (sha256-verified against the frozen WSL dir, same basename) -- see voice.checkpoint.darwin -- and the weights being identical is exactly why this block has to exist separately: a cap is produced by RENDERING, and the render here goes through mlx-audio's sampler rather than vllm-omni's.

mlx._maxCharsNote: 900, CERTIFIED for THIS directory ON THIS BACKEND - the Mac copy of ds_ad4lm_prod_ckpt1080 (sha256-identical to the WSL dir the served certificate binds to) rendered through narrator's own HiggsV3MlxEngine (mlx-audio 0.4.8, mlx 0.32.0, owens-mac-studio) on 2026-09-05T13:19 by the same rule and the same scorer objects as the served certificate (faster-whisper base.en int8 + difflib coverage; babble = coverage < 0.05; babble==0 across all seeds AND min per-seed coverage >= 0.90, contiguous from the shortest): seeds 500-503 x 150/300/600/900/1200/1500; babble 0/4 at every length; min coverage 100.0 / 97.3 / 98.5 / 94.8 at 150/300/600/900, then 1200 FAILS at 83.2% (seed 500 dropped a middle block; the other three seeds passed) and 1500 at 84.4%. The failure mode on MLX is DROPPED TEXT, never babble. NOT the served number: the served path certified 1200 on the identical weights, which is exactly why a certificate is per (directory, backend). Full per-seed table, RTF (0.52-0.62), peak memory (11.3 GiB at 900) and every deviation from the served harness: docs/certificates/max_chars_certificate_mlx_ckpt1080.json.
mlx._samplingNote: A MIRROR OF THE SAME FILE THE SERVED BLOCK MIRRORS, and the DIRECTORY is still the authority -- but on this arm narrator is what applies it. mlx-audio 0.4.8 does not read generation_config.json at all (measured: `grep -rn generation_config tts/models/higgs_audio_v3/` finds nothing, while three other model packages in the same release do read it) and its Model.generate defaults top_p/top_k to None, so narrator's HiggsV3MlxConfig.mlx_sampling() reads <checkpointDir>/generation_config.json itself, through the same v3_served.require_generation_config the served arm uses. The Mac copy carries the same file as the WSL directory: {temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 50, repetition_penalty 1.0}. A repetition_penalty other than 1.0 would be REFUSED here rather than dropped, because mlx-audio has no such lever and honouring the file is impossible on this runtime. tools/test-higgs-engine.js checks this mirror against a fixture generation_config.json -- a mirror nobody checks is how two copies of a number diverge; if they ever disagree, the DIRECTORY wins and this block is what is wrong.

models.note: The deathstalker narrator as a merged Higgs v3 fine-tune. WHY A FINE-TUNE RATHER THAN REFERENCE CLIPS: zero-shot cloning already recovers 92% of the narrator's speaker-identity ceiling (cosine 0.7037 of 0.7656, from a 27.4 s two-clip same-book reference), so TIMBRE is largely solved without training. What cloning does NOT recover is PHRASING — the render places 2.01 pauses per 100 chars against the narrator's 1.39 and runs pitch std 5.17 st against his 4.36, i.e. it performs the text rather than reading it, and no reference, sampling setting or control token moved either number. Only a fine-tune on his phrasing closes that gap, which is what this entry is for — and it is also why Owen ruled on 2026-09-04 that production narration is fine-tuned voices ONLY.
models._cloneFallbackNote: There is deliberately no clips-based deathstalker entry standing in for this one. The measured best zero-shot configuration is a 27.4 s join of cd_cd_00001100.wav + cd_cd_00001951.wav from the ds_ad4s cut with their book-exact transcripts, and it renders well — but those clips live under E:\training and are not a deployable artifact location, so an entry pointing at them would be a voice that works on exactly one machine, which is the failure this catalog exists to prevent. To add one: join the clips to a single wav (0.35 s of silence between them), join the transcripts in the same order, stage both under /home/<user>/higgs-models/<voice>/refs/, and declare ONE clip here with its measured `seconds`.
models._kindNote: kind 'checkpoint' — a MERGED fine-tune directory the server is started on, prompted TEXT-ONLY. No clips key: the voice is in the weights. It was called 'adapter' until 2026-09-04, which described the artifact we trained rather than the artifact that SERVES: vllm-omni has no runtime LoRA path, so the LoRA is an archival input to a merge and never a catalog field.

_checkpointShapeComment: A CHECKPOINT VOICE NAMES ITS MERGED DIRECTORY ONCE PER ARM: `voice.checkpoint: { "wsl": "<absolute guest path>", "darwin": "<path relative to the app's userData>" }`. The single `voice.checkpointDir` string it replaced (retired 2026-09-05) is REFUSED by name if it reappears — one string can only be one machine's path, and it was the WSL guest's, so a Mac render was handed a /home/telltale/... directory that does not exist there and died inside narrator. The keys are the FILESYSTEM the weights sit on, which is why they are not the doctor's HiggsArm vocabulary ('wsl' | 'mlx' | 'none'): that answers which BACKEND was examined, and its third member is a machine no checkpoint can be staged on at all. The two are 1:1 today (wsl<->wsl, darwin<->mlx) and electron/higgs-models.ts is the one place that says so. A MISSING ARM MEANS NOT LOADABLE THERE — never the other arm's path, never a search of the disk: `listRenderableHiggsModels()` and `resolveHiggsModel()` are arm-aware, so the narration dropdown and Listen show a checkpoint voice as loadable only on a machine the catalog stages it for, and higgsVoicesDocument() writes the ONE path for the arm being spawned.
_pathComment: PATHS IN THIS FILE ARE HOST-NATIVE, and they are translated for the guest at DOCUMENT-WRITE time, per spawn arm (see higgsVoicesDocument). An earlier draft stored WSL-native paths and handed them to every arm untranslated, which is correct on the Windows+WSL arm by accident and meaningless on macOS/Linux, where there is no guest to be native to. `toGuestPath` translates a Windows drive path (C:... -> /mnt/c/...) and a \wsl$ UNC (the form tool-paths.ts already documents for orpheusModelsDir) and passes an already-guest-form path through unchanged, so a catalog written on any of the three machines resolves on all of them.
